edges.description: High, homogeneous GD2 expression permits antigen-dependent recognition and killing of glioma cells by GD2-directed CAR T cells. This edge is intervention-conditioned — it is realised only when GD2-CAR T cells are administered.

The infused CAR construct carries murine-derived and engineered junctional sequences that are foreign to the host, so the therapeutic cell product is itself presented as an antigen and provokes an adaptive response against it.
HACA titres vary inversely with circulating CAR T cell persistence, and non-engineered lymphocytes outcompete CAR T cells in the CSF compartment.

nodes.description: Initial clinical and radiographic benefit from GD2-CAR T cells is followed in many patients by loss of durable response and tumour progression. Responses are not uniformly lost - one trial patient remained in complete response beyond 30 months - so this node records a frequent rather than a universal outcome. Appearance of circulating HACA has been temporally associated with disease progression, identifying anti-CAR immunity as a contributor to acquired resistance alongside the GD2-low residual populations seen preclinically.

nodes.description: Recipients mount a host adaptive immune response directed at the CAR construct rather than at the tumour. Peripheral CD4+ and CD8+ T cells react against epitopes concentrated in the murine-derived and engineered junctional regions of the receptor, and cerebrospinal-fluid B cells clonally expand and secrete human anti-CAR antibodies (HACAs) that bind GD2-CAR-expressing cells and impede their cytotoxic activity. This is an immunogenicity mechanism against the therapeutic product, distinct from tumour-intrinsic antigen loss.

evidence.snippet: This was associated with appearance of circulating Human Anti-CAR Antibodies (HACAs) that bound cells expressing the GD2-CAR, as well as clonal expansion of CSF B cells which produced HACA which impeded the cytotoxic activity of GD2-CAR T cells.

nodes.description: Global loss of H3K27me3 causes derepression of genes normally silenced during development, including proliferative and stemness genes. Paradoxically, some loci show retained or increased H3K27me3, suggesting complex redistribution rather than simple loss.

nodes.description: Patient-derived H3 K27M-mutant glioma cells express the disialoganglioside GD2 uniformly and at high levels, at all three midline sites (pons, thalamus and spinal cord). The reported specificity contrast is against H3 wild-type, GD2-negative paediatric glioma cultures, which GD2-CAR T cells do not kill; GD2 expression in normal brain has been reported separately, and the argument for a therapeutic window rests instead on the absence of significant neurotoxicity in human trials using the same 14g2a-derived binding domain. GD2 is synthesised by GD2 synthase (B4GALNT1); CRISPR deletion of B4GALNT1 abolishes GD2-CAR T cell recognition, establishing the ganglioside as the operative surface target rather than a bystander marker. This node is the therapeutic vulnerability that GD2-directed CAR T cell therapy addresses; it is not by itself a driver of tumour growth.

nodes.description: Autologous T cells engineered with a GD2-directed chimeric antigen receptor (GD2 binding domain, 4-1BB co-stimulatory domain, CD3-zeta signalling domain) recognise GD2 on midline glioma cells and mediate antigen-dependent cytotoxicity. In orthotopic xenografts this clears engrafted tumour except for residual GD2-low cells; in the phase I trial it produced volumetric tumour reduction and neurological improvement in a subset of patients. Because the tumour sits in the brainstem or cord, the same inflammatory response produces tumour inflammation-associated neurotoxicity.

evidence.snippet: In five independent patient-derived H3-K27M+ DMG orthotopic xenograft models, systemic administration of GD2-targeted CAR T cells cleared engrafted tumors except for a small number of residual GD2lo glioma cells.

evidence.reference_title: Intravenous and intracranial GD2-CAR T cells for H3K27M(+) diffuse midline gliomas.
evidence.snippet: Four patients demonstrated major volumetric tumour reductions (52, 54, 91 and 100%), with a further three patients exhibiting smaller reductions.

nodes.description: Autologous T cells engineered to express a GD2-directed chimeric antigen receptor (4-1BB co-stimulatory and CD3-zeta signalling domains), given intravenously after lymphodepleting chemotherapy and, in patients with benefit, by subsequent intracerebroventricular infusion. Investigational (phase I, NCT04196413). All treated patients developed tumour inflammation-associated neurotoxicity, which is manageable but requires neurocritical care because of the brainstem or cord location. Durability of response has so far been limited in many patients, though one trial patient remains in complete response beyond 30 months.

nodes.description: Lysine-to-methionine substitution at position 27 of histone H3 (K27M) occurs in H3F3A (encoding H3.3) or HIST1H3B/HIST1H3C (encoding H3.1). Despite being present in only 5-15% of total H3 molecules, the mutant histone acts as a dominant negative, sequestering and inhibiting the PRC2 complex.

nodes.description: GD2-CAR T cells in the cerebrospinal fluid show limited persistence and clonal expansion while non-engineered lymphocytes expand and come to dominate the CSF immune compartment. Circulating HACA levels correlate inversely with circulating CAR T cell persistence, consistent with immune-mediated clearance of the engineered product.

nodes.description: Epigenetic dysregulation prevents normal glial differentiation, maintaining cells in a proliferative, undifferentiated state. This contributes to the aggressive behavior and treatment resistance of these tumors.

The H3 K27M mutant histone binds to and inhibits EZH2, the catalytic subunit of PRC2, which normally trimethylates H3K27. This results in global loss of H3K27me3, a repressive epigenetic mark, leading to aberrant gene activation and loss of cell identity.
